grammar.title: 吗 for yes/no questions
grammar.explanation: Adding 吗 (ma) to the end of any statement turns it into a yes/no question, with no change in word order. 你好吗? means "Are you well?" This is a simpler alternative to verb-不-verb questions — don't combine the two in one sentence.

grammar.title: 太...了 for "too much"
grammar.explanation: 太 (tài) means "too" or "extremely", and adding a sentence-final 了 emphasizes the degree. 太好了! is a common exclamation meaning "Great!" or "That's wonderful!", not a literal complaint.

sentences.en: I want to go the most.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu xiǎng qù, tā ne?
sentences.en: We all want to go, what about him?

sentences.pinyin: Zhège shì wǒ de, nàge ne?
sentences.en: This one is mine, what about that one?
